newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals lower and vulnerable.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals lower and vulnerable.

text.p: The precious metals were hovering just above key price support levels on Wednesday after recent sharp losses and dealers said they threaten to break lower.
"We're getting to critical levels," a London-based dealer said. "If the pressure stays on gold it'll head down to $375 and if silver breaks through support we'll get a sell-off."
Gold fixed at $380.30 an ounce, compared to $381.70 on Tuesday afternoon and a London close of $381.30/$381.80.

Prices were holding just above the key $380 an ounce support level after tumbling in a New York-led sell-off on Tuesday afternoon. "Gold as an entity is not looking too well. There has been some quality selling -- not just speculative -- that's pushed the price down," a dealer said.
"Whether it's from producer or central banks we've yet to see," he added.

Unconfirmed rumours of further European central bank selling of gold reserves, as European Union countries seek to meet the 1999 single-currency criteria, has been depressing market sentiment, dealers said.
And recent U.S. economic news easing some fears of inflation and a U.S. interest rate hike have left the market vulnerable to speculative selling, some analysts said.
Business was mostly quiet, but further weakness may attract more speculative interest, dealers said. "If we see more weakness we might see the funds coming on board," one said.
Silver was holding just above its $4.80 support level after crumbling nearly 10 cents on Tuesday afternoon. It was indicated at $4.81/$4.83 and ounce.

Its fate may depend on gold's ability to hang on above support, analysts said. "If gold can stabilise then there are better chances for silver to go up again," said analyst Hanspeter Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corp in Zurich.
"The fundamentals for silver are not that bad." Platinum was trawling the very bottom of its recent $380-$390 price range, fixing at a fresh near-three year low of $380.50 an ounce.
Palladium was also weak and close to support levels at $115.25/$116.25 an ounce, although it was up about $0.75 from lows hit at Tuesday's London close.
Platinum and palladium have been sliding lower in recent months under pressure from ample supply from key producer Russia and slack demand from the key Japanese electronics industry.
